question_text: Find the equation of the straight line parallel to the line 2x+3y+7=0 and passing through the point (5,4).

mark_split.label: Write the line through the point

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what the slope must be, and which form you would use.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the required slope
steps.margin_note: First mark. Read the given line's slope off its coefficients as −a/b, then keep it, because parallel lines share a slope.
steps.memory_tip: Read the given slope off as −a/b and KEEP it — parallel lines share a slope.
lines: (the slope of ax + by + c = 0 is −a/b; here a = 2, b = 3)
A parallel line has the same slope,

recall.must_convey: That the given slope is found as −a/b and the required slope is the same.
accept: parallel lines have the same slope
read minus a over b and use it as is

steps.why: The slope is fixed entirely by the other line, so it can be written before the given point is used at all.
common_mistakes: Taking the negative reciprocal when the lines are parallel.

steps.label: Write the line through the point
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Point-slope form, then clear the fraction and collect. A shorter one-line method for this type is given below.
steps.memory_tip: Point-slope form, then clear the fraction and collect.

lines.text: (the point-slope form, with (x₁, y₁) = (5, 4) and m = −2/3)
(a line parallel to ax + by + c = 0 has the same a and b)

lines: The parallel line is given by  a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) = 0

recall.must_convey: That the point-slope form through the given point gives 2x + 3y − 22 = 0.
accept: use y minus y one equals m into x minus x one then simplify
write the point slope form and clear the fraction
put the point and slope in and collect the terms
point slope form lo pettesi simplify cheyyali

steps.why: The shorter method works because a parallel line keeps the same coefficients in the same places, so only the constant has to be recomputed.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the right side by 3 and writing y − 4 = −2(x − 5).
Leaving the answer with a fraction in it.
lines_compact: The parallel line is given by  a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) = 0

insider_note: A shorter method does not need the slope: a parallel line through (x₁, y₁) is a(x − x₁) + b(y − y₁) = 0, so 2(x − 5) + 3(y − 4) = 0 reaches the answer with no fractions at all.
